recentItems.title: Russia claims gains in Donetsk as maps show conflicting realities
recentItems.description:
Russia has spent this year pushing to capture the remaining parts of Donetsk, with military bloggers describing the situation around Lyman as “difficult” and fighting as intense, but not a retreat. Official maps tell competing stories: TASS shows Lyman and nearby towns under Russian control, while Ukraine’s Deep State says they are Ukrainian-held. 

Al Jazeera's Dmitry Medvedenko reports from Moscow.

recentItems.title: Ukraine regains ground in east as counteroffensive challenges stalemate narrative
recentItems.description:
Ukraine says its forces have retaken at least 125 square kilometres of territory near the eastern city of Lyman, following a largely unpublicised counteroffensive by the 3rd Army Corps. Independent analysts have estimated that more than 200 square kilometres may have been recaptured during the four-month operation, though official information remains limited.
The area is strategically important because Lyman lies north of Kramatorsk and Slovyansk, the last major Donbas cities that Russia is seeking to capture. Ukraine’s advance could ease pressure on the cities by disrupting Russia’s attempt to encircle them from the north and south. While the gains do not amount to a major breakthrough, they challenge the perception that the front line has remained entirely static.

Al Jazeera’s Rory Challands reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.

recentItems.title: Cambodia scam crackdown drives cybercrime networks worldwide: Expert
recentItems.description:
Cambodia says it has shut down 800 suspected online scam sites, but criminal networks may have simply moved elsewhere.

Jason Tower, a senior expert at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, told Al Jazeera that cyber-scams had become a major part of Cambodia’s economy by 2023, with some reports estimating the criminal market at about 40 percent of GDP.

He said the closures amounted to a “mass clearance operation” rather than the full dismantling of the industry, as many suspected operators left the country. Tower warned that scam syndicates are expanding into South Asia, Africa and the Middle East.

recentItems.title: War on Iran drives up food prices and malnutrition risk in Nigeria
recentItems.description:
The US-Israel war on Iran is pushing up food and fuel costs in Nigeria, where many families are already struggling to afford basic meals. Health workers warn rising living costs are putting more people, particularly children, at risk of malnutrition. Farmers say expensive fertiliser, labour and other inputs are forcing them to raise prices. Fuel prices also rose by about 50 percent in many parts of Nigeria days after the war began, while transport costs remain high. 

Al Jazeera's Ahmed Idris reports from Bodinga, Nigeria.

recentItems.title: Israel’s wars reshape the middle east as UN rules lose their grip
recentItems.description:
Israel’s war in Gaza and attacks across Palestine, Lebanon, Syria, Yemen and Iraq have helped turn one conflict into several, with open waters now used as choke points. Iran has invoked Article 51 of the UN Charter, sending missiles and drones far beyond recognized battlefields and linking strikes in one country to responses in others. As Israel keeps testing how far it can go, the question is whether the international system can adapt before the rules remain only on paper. 

Al Jazeera's Osama Bin Javaid reports from the United Nations headquarters in New York.

recentItems.title: Six months of war push Iran’s economy to breaking point
recentItems.description:
More than six months of war have left Iran’s economy under intense strain, forcing families to choose what they can still afford and what they must live without. Years of sanctions are compounded by a plunging currency of about 2 million rials to the dollar, 65% inflation and food prices up 128%. Shopkeepers in Tehran say imports are scarce and customers are cutting back as war damage nears an estimated $270bn and tens of thousands of homes and public services are hit. While control over the Strait of Hormuz gives Iran some leverage, millions of Iranians face a more immediate question: how long they can bear the cost. 

Al Jazeera's Sinem Koseoglu reports from Tehran.

recentItems.title: Shield of the Americas targets 24 “narcoterrorist” groups
recentItems.description:
Just months after its creation, the US‑led Shield of the Americas has outlined its first joint move: asking members to treat 24 criminal organizations as terrorist groups. The plan would extend US sanctions, asset freezes and prosecutions across the region, even as key powers like Brazil and Mexico stay out over sovereignty concerns. Rights advocates warn lethal US strikes on suspected drug boats may breach international law. 

Al Jazeera's Alessandro Rampietti reports from Bogota.
